extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, trademark practitioners, and attorneys/agents who practice before the USPTO; OED and regulatory counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO disciplinary rules, statutory prohibitions, and procedural requirements governing the conduct of practitioners (attorneys/agents) before the USPTO, and the sanctions/publication procedures applied when those rules are violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) — disreputable or gross misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a practitioner from engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as a basis for discipline where practitioner assisted in unauthorized practice and divided fees with an Office employee; used to evaluate whether conduct is sufficiently serious to warrant suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — dishonesty, fraud, deceit, misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a practitioner from engaging in conduct that involves dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where practitioner's conduct involved facilitating unauthorized practice and sharing fees with an employee of the Office; used as an element to establish unprofessional/ethical breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) — prejudicial to administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a practitioner from engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant when practitioner actions undermine the integrity or proper functioning of USPTO processes (e.g., enabling an employee to continue representing private clients).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — adversely reflects on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a practitioner from engaging in conduct that adversely reflects upon the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess whether misconduct casts doubt on the practitioner's continued qualification to represent clients before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.37 — fee division restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a practitioner from dividing a fee with another who is not a partner or associate of the practitioner's law firm without the consent of the client after full disclosure, and requires the total fee not be excessive and be shared proportionally to the services performed by each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation example: collecting legal fees and sharing them with a non-lawyer (or non-partner/non-associate) such as an Office employee; evaluation includes whether client consent, full disclosure, proportional sharing, and non-excessive fee requirements were met.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.47(c) — aiding unauthorized practice of law
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits a practitioner from aiding a non-lawyer in the unauthorized practice of law before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where a registered practitioner assisted an individual (e.g., an Office employee not qualified to practice) to continue representing clients before the USPTO, including providing substantive services or sharing fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(c) — inactivation and withdrawal upon USPTO employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires that upon becoming employed by the Office, an individual must administratively inactivate his/her registration to practice before the Office and withdraw from all matters then pending before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to administratively inactivate and to withdraw from pending representations (e.g., an examiner who continued to have 'clients') is a regulatory violation and can trigger disciplinary action against any practitioner who aids that continued representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 18 U.S.C. §§ 203 and 205 — federal prohibitions on employee representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutes that preclude employees of the Office from prosecuting or aiding in any manner in the prosecution of any patent application or application for trademark registration before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These criminal/conflict-of-interest statutes are cited when an Office employee continued to act for private clients; practitioners who facilitate such activity risk discipline and referral; also used to show the seriousness of the misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 2.17(a) — trademark representation eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an individual qualified to practice under § 11.14 may represent an applicant, registrant, or party to a proceeding before the Office in a trademark case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited to show that an Office employee (or any unqualified individual) is not authorized to represent trademark clients; assisting such representation violates USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional authority for discipline — 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D), 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory and regulatory provisions that give the USPTO Director jurisdiction over practitioner disciplinary matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the Office's authority to investigate, settle, and impose sanctions for practitioner misconduct; procedural foundation for final orders and settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 — notice/publication of public discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires the OED Director to give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically implemented by publishing the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and issuing a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette; used both as a sanction mechanism and public notice requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and limited recognition for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory framework governing limited recognition/reinstatement procedures; the Order grants limited recognition for a short period (45 days) solely to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to permit narrowly-limited practice for administrative compliance (e.g., to wrap up matters necessary for compliance with reinstatement procedures); the practitioner must comply with the detailed requirements of § 11.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Order requires the USPTO to promptly dissociate the practitioner's name from all USPTO customer numbers and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) certificates; practitioner may not use any customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical restriction preventing access to USPTO electronic systems during suspension; serves as an enforceable part of the suspension sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary decision in OED Reading Room and Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the Final Order be published electronically in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and that a Notice of Suspension be published in the Official Gazette, materially consistent with the provided notice text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures public disclosure of the discipline and the factual and legal basis; part of the remedial/transparent discipline process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may consider prior disciplinary record as aggravating or rebuttal evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct, and/or in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by or on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns practitioners that settled matters may be used against them in future proceedings, affecting severity of subsequent sanctions.
